title: Baptismal Font
description: A medieval stone baptismal font with rounded arches and stylized male heads.
museum_label: Water from Heaven. Every medieval church had a baptistery with a font with holy water. By pouring the water onto people, they became part of the Catholic church. This was of the utmost importance, as only the baptized would go to heaven after death. This baptismal font, with stylized male heads between rounded arches, probably dates from the 13th Century. Early 20th Century it was restored from fragments of Romanesque sculpture, found amongst debris of stonemasonry. The debris originated from a church near Nijmegen, possibly Batenburg, which still holds a similar baptismal font. From the 1920s, this font was used as a planter in gardens of houses in Bois-le-Duc, Vught and Eindhoven, before it was donated to the museum in 2016.

description: A burial find connected to ritual and daily life.

title: Roman Glass Vessel
description: A glass vessel showing Roman influence and material culture.
museum_label: This glass vessel reflects Roman influence and the spread of new materials. Its fragile shape helps visitors think about trade, luxury, and local adoption.
